solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: No, It is opposition also from the east that makes this!

definitions.text: No, It is opposition also from the east that makes this!

parts.words: No, It is opposition also from the east that makes this
parts.note: the phrase in front of the solver spells exactly the same letters whether read from the left or from the right, from the east

explanation.surface: Someone protests 'No, it is opposition!' and is told that coming from the east makes it something special.
explanation.walkthrough: Write NO IT IS OPPOSITION as one run of letters and read it right to left ('from the east'): it is unchanged, so the clue is itself an example of what it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase reading identically in both directions is the very thing the clue's own opening words demonstrate.

clue.text: How the secrets came out altogether

definitions.meaning: secrets that all got told came out completely

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'in total' and, read literally, describes every secret having been disclosed.

clue.text: Arab leaders of intifada resent anyone questioning it

indicators.note: the leaders of a set of words are their opening letters, one from each word that follows

explanation.surface: Arab activists of the intifada bristle at anyone who challenges the uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Iraq is a national of an Arab country, so an Arab is a fair example-style definition.

clue.text: Mine follows detailed ruling, being old and feeble

indicators.note: the word for mine comes after the shortened ruling
de-tailed: the word for ruling loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: a decree is an official ruling
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A mine operates under an elaborate regulation even though the place is old and falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'elaborate' but splits as de-tailed: the ruling loses its final E, and 'follows' puts the mine after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes someone worn out and weakened by age, matching old and feeble exactly.

clue.text: Tidy soldier could be in a mess

definitions.text: Tidy soldier could be in a mess

parts.note: orderly means neat and tidy
a sergeant is a non-commissioned soldier

explanation.surface: A neat soldier might still end up in the mess hall, or in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the duty NCO, who would be found in the sergeants' mess, a military dining room; the blogger noted the slight overlap of 'soldier' with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An orderly sergeant is the NCO on daily duty, a soldier who eats in the sergeants' mess.

clue.text: Old rupee convertible in some 50 countries here

indicators.note: a convertible currency can be changed, here into a new arrangement of letters

explanation.surface: An old rupee can be exchanged for the money used across dozens of nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' sounds like a currency term, but it tells you to rearrange O plus RUPEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent contains roughly fifty sovereign states, so it is where some fifty countries are found.

clue.text: Flat number showing here cancels opening

indicators.note: the first letter of the number is struck out

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A flat's number displayed here wipes out the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat number' wants to be a house number; 'Flat' alone is the definition and 'number' gives SEVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Even is a synonym of level or smooth, as a flat surface is.

clue.text: Non-fat feast with loads, say, of French food

indicators.note: the letters spelling fat are removed from the word they precede

parts.note: taken as written before the letters are removed

indicators.note: signals that the next piece only sounds like the word for loads

parts.note: cargoes are loads carried by ships

explanation.surface: A low-fat banquet with plenty of French dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing F, A and T from FEAST leaves ES; CARGOTS, with its silent French T, is said like CARGOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargots are snails cooked as a classic dish of French cuisine.

clue.text: Private Cox easily carries around one of these missiles

annotationWithheld.why: Private Cox easily carries around one of these missiles (7): the reversed hidden run in privaTE COX Easily gives the singular EXOCET (6), 'one of these'; no clue word supplies the plural's final S, so no wp builds the 7-letter answer.
annotationWithheld.clue: Private Cox easily carries around one of these missiles

clue.text: What appeal could also mean with a third off

definitions.text: What appeal could also mean with a third off

parts.words: What appeal could also mean with a third off
parts.note: take two of the six letters, A and P, away from the word appeal and rearrange the rest into a word that also means appeal

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a word for a request might mean once trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: APPEAL loses a third of its letters (A and P) and the remaining PEAL is rearranged, though no word signals the rearrangement, so the clue works as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest request, a synonym for an appeal.

clue.text: Doctor Rice set out to be top business partner

indicators.note: the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A medic called Rice sets off to become a senior partner in a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A codirector shares the running of a company with another, a senior business partner.

clue.text: Stay as guest of Her Majesty, perhaps

definitions.text: Stay as guest of Her Majesty, perhaps

parts.words: Stay as guest of Her Majesty, perhaps
parts.note: being detained at Her Majesty's pleasure means serving a prison sentence, not visiting the palace

explanation.surface: An invitation to stay with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: British prisons were HM Prisons, so a 'guest of Her Majesty' is a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means serving a prison term, a stay in one of the monarch's jails.

clue.text: A revolutionary olde-worlde for every journalist

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: retro means deliberately old-fashioned in style
per means for each, for every

explanation.surface: A radical old-fashioned type for every newspaper writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a description of a person, but it turns both pieces right round as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and writes news stories.

clue.text: A mostly innocent sort of parade

definitions.text: A mostly innocent sort of parade

parts.words: A mostly innocent sort of parade
parts.note: a police line-up consists mostly of innocent people with one suspect among them

explanation.surface: A procession whose members are largely blameless.
explanation.walkthrough: In an identity parade, a police line-up, all but one of the people are innocent volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity parade is a police line-up, nearly all of whose members are innocent stand-ins.

clue.text: Slightest quarrel occurs in breeding location

indicators.note: the bolt is placed inside the nesting place

parts.note: a nest is where birds breed
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: The faintest argument breaks out in a nesting colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' wants to mean a row, but here it is a crossbow bolt, and 'occurs in' puts it inside the breeding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowest means smallest in margin, as in the slightest or narrowest of wins.

clue.text: Sunday lunch not right for this kind of oven

indicators.note: a dish that is not right is missing something, here the letter standing for right

parts.note: a roast is the traditional British Sunday lunch

explanation.surface: Sunday lunch isn't right for an oven of this type.
explanation.walkthrough: A roast dinner is the traditional British Sunday meal; dropping R gives a kiln for drying hops.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln used to dry hops, a kind of oven.

clue.text: Cheers for Hitchcock's double feature

definitions.meaning: a toast said when raising glasses
the film director Alfred Hitchcock had a noticeably double chin, two facial features

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old toast like 'cheers', and also a double chin such as Hitchcock's.

clue.text: Police officer or fashion icon

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A choice between a policeman and a famous fashion figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was a celebrated French couturier whose house remains a fashion name.

clue.text: West African's first to be deposed by a Portuguese?

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a Liberian comes from Liberia in West Africa

explanation.surface: A West African leader is overthrown by a man from Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposed' suggests a coup, but it takes L off LIBERIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal lies on the Iberian peninsula, so a Portuguese person is an example of an Iberian.

clue.text: A ship ENE, roughly, of old Turkish town

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about, as a ship in rough water

explanation.surface: A ship sailing east-northeast near an ancient Turkish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient city in modern Turkey; its adjective describes things from that town.

clue.text: An unplaced racehorse may be too controlled

parts.note: also means too, as well
ran means managed or controlled

explanation.surface: A horse that failed to finish in the frame may be over-managed too.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse that runs but does not finish among the placed runners.

clue.text: Two fellows seduced by a lot of nonsense

indicators.note: being seduced means being taken in, so the pair goes inside

parts.note: a pile is a large amount
F is the abbreviation for fellow, doubled

explanation.surface: Two men are taken in by a great deal of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffle is trivial nonsense, silly talk.

clue.text: Turning out to be attractive

definitions.meaning: ... as in growing into or getting to be
... as in flattering or suiting someone

explanation.definitionFit: Becoming means coming to be, and also flattering or attractive, as a becoming dress.

clue.text: Turning brown is, with time, totally possible for club member

indicators.note: the colour word is turned round

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Getting a tan is quite possible for a member of the right club, all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totally possible' hints at an all-over tan, which is why the blogger read the whole clue as the definition; the defining words are 'club member'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a naturist club goes without clothes, the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Speak slowly to portray ultimate self-control

parts.note: draw means depict or portray

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the very last one

explanation.surface: Talk slowly to show the utmost self-discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate self-control' looks like a phrase about discipline, but it gives the last letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: To drawl is to speak with drawn-out, lazily slow vowels.

clue.text: Much-married lady with a story to tell

definitions.text: Much-married lady with a story to tell

parts.words: Much-married lady with a story to tell
parts.note: Chaucer's pilgrim who had five husbands tells one of the Canterbury Tales

explanation.surface: A woman married many times has a tale to share.
explanation.walkthrough: In Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, a medieval English poem, this pilgrim has had five husbands and tells her own tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's pilgrim narrator had five husbands and recounts a story on the road to Canterbury.

clue.text: Broadcasts put on by the pretentious

definitions.meaning: showy people put on affected manners

explanation.definitionFit: To air is to transmit; affected manners are what snobs are said to give themselves.

clue.text: An insect's taste repels

indicators.note: to repel is to push back, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste

explanation.surface: An insect's flavour drives others away.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, a type of insect.

clue.text: Fishing net, damaged at first, getting caught up

indicators.note: the rearranged net comes before the fishing word
the net is torn and its letters rearranged

parts.note: angling is fishing with a rod and line

explanation.surface: A fishing net, damaged early on, gets snagged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges NET into ENT, which 'at first' places before the fishing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Entangling means becoming caught or twisted up in something.
